Republican incumbent [[Olympia Snowe]] was re-elected to a second term in a landslide over Democratic state senator [[Mark Lawrence (politician)|Mark Lawrence]]. == General election == === Candidates === * [[Mark Lawrence (politician)|Mark W. Lawrence]], state senator from [[Kittery, Maine|Kittery]] and former president of the [[Maine Senate]] (Democratic) * [[Olympia Snowe]], incumbent U.S. senator since 1995 (Republican) === Campaign === Snowe, a popular moderate incumbent,{{cite news |last1=Crowley |first1=Michael |last2=Kranish |first2=Michael |title=New England: Big prize gets little attention |url=https://cache.boston.com/news/politics/campaign2000/news/New_England_Big_prize_gets_little_attention+.shtml |access-date=24 January 2020 |work=[[Boston Globe]] |date=February 27, 2000}} outpolled and outspent Lawrence.{{Cite web |last=Favinger |first=Larry |title=Mark Lawrence puts bold foot forward in campaign |url=https://www.seacoastonline.com/story/news/2000/10/17/mark-lawrence-puts-bold-foot/51304762007/ |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=Portsmouth Herald |language=en-US}} === Debates === The two candidates agreed to debate on October 15 and 25.{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=J9JKAAAAIBAJ&sjid=a_MMAAAAIBAJ&pg=1355,3298735 |work=[[Sun Journal (Lewiston, Maine)|Sun Journal]] |title=Snowe-Lawrence debate will be rebroadcast |date=October 18, 2000 |page=A2|via=[[Google News Archive]]}} === Polling === {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign="bottom" ! scope="col" |Poll source ! scope="col" |Date(s) ! scope="col" style="width:75px;" |Sample
